StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

DisplayAmount.rationale: TenderPower.cs:22 shows CardsPlayedThisTurn instead of Amount. The sim keeps the counter separately (`_cards_played_this_turn`, powers.py:2110) but has no display concept. Presentation.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: The applier is dropped. TenderPower.cs:50-51 applies Strength and Dexterity -1 with `applier: base.Applier` -- the creature that applied Tender -- and `silent: true`; powers.py:2115-2116 calls PowerCmd.apply with no applier at all. DORMANT but with a real route: PossessStrengthPower and PossessSpeedPower (powers.py:3075-3147) track stat losses BY APPLIER (`applier is self.owner`, powers.py:3094) so they can hand the stats back on death. A monster holding Possess Strength that also applied Tender would, in the game, be credited with the Tender drain and return it; in the sim the drain is applier-less and is lost. Both powers are ported (Hunter Killer applies Tender, The Lost/The Forgotten hold the Possess powers). Named trigger: one monster applying Tender while another holds a Possess power, or any single monster with both. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.maps_to: powers.py:2118-2124 on_player_turn_end restores the drained stats
AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called for the player side at CombatManager.cs:1307 -- AFTER the turn-end card effects and the hand flush. The sim's on_player_turn_end is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (combat.py:654), before _process_turn_end_cards (combat.py:658) and before the flush (:661-662); the sim's real AfterTurnEnd slot, after_player_turn_end (combat.py:665), is available and unused. The concrete route for this whole group: StampedePower (powers.py:1025-1041) auto-plays Attacks from ITS on_player_turn_end, so in the game every turn-end auto-play happens while this power is still on the creature and in the sim that depends on registration order. Reproduce with `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots`. Third-file citations, not hashed here. LIVE for this unit: Tender restores Strength and Dexterity at turn end, and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays are Attack plays whose damage scales off Strength. In the game the restore happens AFTER them, so those attacks are still Tenderised; in the sim it happens in the same dispatch, so whether they are depends on registration order between Tender and Stampede. The restore also uses the same applier-less PowerCmd.apply as the drain, so it cannot be credited either.

guards.what: TenderPower.cs:50-51 the literal -1 per card, regardless of Amount
guards.rationale: powers.py:2115-2116 applies -1 for each of Strength and Dexterity, not -Amount. Matches C#, whose Amount is only the display anchor -- the kind of constant that is easy to 'fix' wrongly and the sim did not.

guards.what: TenderPower.cs:59-60 restores CardsPlayedThisTurn, then zeroes it
guards.rationale: powers.py:2122-2124 applies +_cards_played_this_turn to both stats and then resets. Exact, including restoring the COUNT rather than Amount, so the net effect over a turn is zero on both sides.

guards.what: TenderPower.cs:55-62 fires even when no card was played
guards.rationale: C# calls PowerCmd.Apply with CardsPlayedThisTurn == 0; the sim guards `self._cards_played_this_turn == 0 -> return` (powers.py:2119-2120). Equivalent, and this time the equivalence is exact rather than lucky: C# PowerCmd.Apply returns immediately on `amount == 0m` (PowerCmd.cs:103), so a 0-amount application is a documented no-op -- step 6 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
